name: Pan-Finnicism
summary: Pan-Finnicism (heimoaate, "kinship idea") holds that the Finnic or wider Finno-Ugric peoples share language and ancestry and should work toward cultural, economic or political union, usually with Finland in the lead. In its strongest form it fused with Greater Finland irredentism, seeking Karelia and other kin lands from Russia, and it was hostile to Russian rule and later Soviet power. It is a pan-nationalism of kinship by language and descent, with no economic doctrine of its own.
scope: The Finland-centred mainstream from Fennoman roots (Topelius 1844, Castrén, Ahlqvist) through the interwar heimoaate and Greater Finland current (Academic Karelia Society, kinship wars) to its peak in the Winter and Continuation Wars. Excludes Hungarian Turanism as a separate current, and the marginal modern cultural Finno-Ugric congress movement except where noted. Economic, social and moral questions are mostly inferred from the interwar Finnish nationalist milieu and are low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Zachris Topelius
keyFigures.role: Wrote the 1844 essay imagining a future Pan-Fennicism led by the Finns.

keyFigures.name: Matthias Castrén
keyFigures.role: Philologist whose Finno-Ugric and Altaic kinship theories underpinned the idea.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Kinship nationalism says nothing on health systems; its Finnish adherents ranged from agrarian to conservative, so there is no stated lean either way.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage-setting never figured in Fennoman or Greater Finland programmes; the question is outside what unites the kin-peoples idea.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement's sources discuss language, kinship and territory, not market economics, and adherents did not share one economic doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Academic Karelia Society's hostility to socialists and communists; public ownership was a socialist demand, though nationalist states also nationalised.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position; the cause drew support across classes and its programme is silent on taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from interwar adherents' strong hostility to socialists; unions of that era were tied to the socialist left that the Karelia Society opposed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred from anti-communist stance and rural-nationalist outlook; property rights are never discussed as a kinship matter.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not an issue for kin-peoples nationalism; no source links the idea to corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare policy is not part of the idea; adherents' views followed their broader party politics.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the anti-socialist, class-collaborationist nationalism of the Academic Karelia Society; no source addresses cooperatives.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the interwar adherents' security-minded anti-Soviet and anti-communist outlook; no source addresses surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not discussed; conservative-nationalist adherents of the era would be expected to favour prohibition.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents' own slogans were hostile to Russians and socialists, but a nationalist movement would back legal limits on speech seen as harming the nation.

strong-leader.rationale: The Karelia Society grew ambivalent then opposed to democracy, and Estonian kin-movement politics ended in authoritarian rule; adherents split, with the interwar mainstream leaning to firm leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: The idea aims at building or enlarging a state (Greater Finland), so adherents treat the state as essential, not harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Volunteer expeditions and the paramilitary Civil Guard culture of the era make strict gun limits unlikely to appeal; inferred, not stated.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Academic Karelia Society pressed for a stronger army, and irredentist aims rest on military strength.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed; traditional-nationalist adherents of the interwar peak would oppose.

decide-locally.rationale: Greater Finland and pan-Finnic union centralise kin peoples in one state; Snellman-style unitary national-state thinking underlies the Fennoman roots.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy never entered kin-peoples nationalism, and interwar adherents ranged from liberal Fennomans to hardliners, so the idea itself leans neither way.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-nationalist milieu and the Lutheran missions that spread the idea in Karelia; the sources do not state a family doctrine.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for a 19th-20th century idea; inferred from its conservative-nationalist adherents.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the pro-natal, nation-strengthening outlook and Lutheran ties of its Finnish supporters; abortion was not a topic in any source on the idea.

more-religion-public.rationale: Lutheran missions spread the idea in Russian Karelia and the Karelia Society's oath invokes God, but religion is not the idea's core.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's concern is Finnic kinship, and it ranked Finno-Ugric peoples above East Slavs in practice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-nationalist and Lutheran milieu of its adherents in the 19th and early 20th centuries; the sources do not discuss gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The cause began as a cultural project to unite kin through language, folklore and shared heritage, and Karelianism treated Karelian culture as the national wellspring.

gradual-change.rationale: Irredentist and uprising-oriented, so poorly matched with gradualism; but Fennomania itself was a patient cultural programme.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from ethnic-nation logic; immigration was not a live question in the idea's main periods.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The idea is a nation-and-kin project; world bodies like the UN did not exist in its peak, and sovereignty-minded nationalists would not expand them.

free-trade.rationale: The idea concerns language kinship and borders rather than commerce, and its supporters held no common line on tariffs or free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Pan-Finnicism is a cooperation among kin peoples led by Finland's interests, not global cooperation; the Finnish nation was to lead.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Volunteers intervened across borders for kin they saw as oppressed, but framed it as kinship duty rather than human rights, so only loosely matching.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred; the idea unites kin peoples but does not call for open borders among all, and nationalists favour defined borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred only: an expansionist, nation-building programme leans against deliberate economic limits, though no source on the idea mentions growth or environment.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is anachronistic for an idea at its peak in 1918-1944, and nothing in its sources links kinship politics to the environment.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Neither Fennoman philology nor interwar Greater Finland propaganda made claims about technology, so there is no position to infer.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for the idea's peak and has no link to kinship or territory, so adherents are not placed on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Castrén imagined revolt against Russian rule with other non-Russian peoples, and kin uprisings were backed later; inferred for revolution against foreign rule only.

experts-over-public.rationale: Philologists like Castrén and Ahlqvist supplied the idea's scholarly base, but no source states a view on expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from anti-Soviet, anti-communist adherents; planning was not discussed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from opposition to socialism; the idea is silent on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not a kinship-nationalist matter; interwar adherents' tax views followed their party politics, not the idea.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is not addressed by pan-Finnic sources, and supporters were spread across parties.

basic-income.rationale: A late-20th-century policy that the idea's sources could not have addressed, with no principle in kin-union thinking pointing either way.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Pan-Finnicism's economic side is only the vague aim of kin economic unification (per the definition), not a protectionist programme.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The sources on the idea describe cultural and territorial aims, not industrial policy, so no stance can be derived.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred from the rural, Karelianist romanticism and Finland's smallholder society; not stated as doctrine.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred from rejection of communism by the Karelia Society and Finnish adherents.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A fringe monetary question that no pan-Finnic source touches; a state-building nationalism would simply keep national institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Interwar adherents drew on ultra-right currents, some corporatist, but no source ties the idea to it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Interwar adherents included authoritarians, but single-party rule is not part of the idea and Finland remained multiparty.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Topelius and other Fennomans were loyal to the tsar while Greater Finland supporters later favoured a republic; adherents were split.

democracy-best.rationale: The Karelia Society was ambivalent about democracy and under Helanen came to oppose it; the early Fennoman movement was not democratic either.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from the Karelia Society's turn against democracy; direct votes are not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers' councils are a Soviet-model form; the society was hostile to socialists, communists and Soviet Russia.

right-to-secede.rationale: Greater Finland supporters backed Karelian and Ingrian separation from Russia (s2), but wanted a Greater Finland kept whole, so support for secession was selective rather than a general principle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Topelius wanted Finns in the lead of a pan-Finnic community, but a doctrine of natural rulers is not stated.

political-violence-never.rationale: Pan-Finnic expeditions and kinship wars were organised violence for political aims, and the idea's peak was military.

war-builds-character.rationale: The idea peaked in the Winter and Continuation Wars and inspired volunteer wars; inferred as romantic militarism, not a stated claim.

separate-church-state.rationale: Lutheran missions spread the idea in Karelia; not strictly separationist but not clerical either.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Protestant-national outlook, not theocratic; the idea defines the nation by language and ancestry.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from the state-building focus; private defence is contrary to the army-building emphasis of the Karelia Society.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from irredentist aims and the push for a stronger army; no source states a doctrine of superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Greater Finland aimed at combining all Finnic peoples into one state, on ethnic-kinship grounds.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Karelia Society was hostile to socialists and communists and put nation and kin above class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred from a nationalism that put kinship and nation above class and was hostile to socialist egalitarian programmes (Karelia Society).

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Kin peoples are treated as holding ancestral lands (Karelia as ancestral home); the idea extends this to Finno-Ugric peoples, not the Sami specifically.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The idea concerns Finnic kin under Russian rule, not overseas colonies, and it never raised reparations; inferred disagreement from nationalist priorities.

civilizational-union.rationale: Kin unity is by language family and descent, and Castrén widened it to Altaic peoples; shared religion or civilization is not the criterion, hence only loosely agree.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Karelia Society's oath pledges work and life to the Fatherland, framing national duty above self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Karelia Society's oath pledged members' work and lives to the Fatherland and Greater Finland.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Karelianism romanticised landscape and folk culture, but intrinsic value of nature is not stated.

limit-population.rationale: Kin peoples were small, and pan-Finnic unity was partly about strength in numbers; inferred only.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Karelianism romanticised the pre-industrial folk but the idea is modernising, nation-building; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The idea's sources are silent on technological change, and Karelianism's romantic folk emphasis gives no clear lean either way.

human-enhancement.rationale: Biotechnology is anachronistic for the idea's historical peak and it offers no principle bearing on it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; nationalist-romantic idea would not hand governing to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is anachronistic for the idea's historical period and unrelated to kinship politics.

restore-past-order.rationale: Karelianism looks back to ancestral roots, but the programme is forward-looking state-building, not restoration of a lost social order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: Pan-Finnicism rests on a primordial, ideological view of ethnicity and kinship (per Shabaev and Mironova) rather than on pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: Volunteer expeditions and uprisings were direct action by kin supporters, though parliament was also used.

means-match-ends.rationale: Adherents used volunteer expeditions and armed uprisings to pursue kin unity, so they did not match methods to a desired peaceful end-state; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: the idea is about modern state-building and kin unity, with Karelian culture romanticised but not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of communism; no pan-Finnic source discusses the division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from the Karelia Society's hostility to communists; the maxim is Marxist and not part of the kin-peoples idea.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from anti-socialist stance of interwar adherents; the idea itself has no production doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred from the Karelia Society's hostility to Marxism and its class-collaboration nationalism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Interwar adherents were hostile to communists and Soviet Russia, the idea's chief opponent.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from anti-Soviet stance; the Soviet collective farm was the opposing model.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred from anti-Marxism; pan-Finnic writers blamed Russia and Soviet power, not capitalism, for the region's conflicts.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: a movement aiming to build and expand a state needs taxation and would not call it theft.

harm-principle.rationale: No source ties the idea to a liberal harm principle, and adherents were happy to restrict socialists, so it is a neutral placeholder.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The idea rests on peoples and kin groups as bearers of identity and claims, with a primordial view of ethnicity.

conscription.rationale: The Karelia Society wanted a stronger army and Finland kept conscription through its irredentist period.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: nationalists emphasise belonging to a homeland and peoples' right to political voice and unity, not leaving as the main check.

state-as-business.rationale: The idea treats the nation-state as a kin community with duties (Karelia Society oath), not a firm with customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material preconditions of freedom are not discussed in any source on the idea.

media-academia-power.rationale: Scholars shaped the idea (Castrén, Ahlqvist), but no source states a claim that universities and media outrank elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Turanist claims included racial kinship, but Pan-Finnicism as documented is mainly linguistic and does not argue about racial ability differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Some interwar adherents had corporatist leanings but no source ties it to the idea.

total-state.rationale: Authoritarian tendencies among interwar adherents, but no total-state doctrine; the idea is about kin unity.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Karelia Society's oath speaks of Finnish national awakening, but it frames this as awakening, not decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Members swore to give their work and lives for Karelia, Ingria and 'great Finland', territories beyond the Finnish state of the day.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: Karelia Society members swore oaths to a Fatherland and flag rather than to a lord, a modern national loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred: a modern nation-building idea with no feudal elements; no source mentions bound labor.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Scholars saw their philology as science showing real kinship, though later scholars call the concept a cultural myth.

universal-morality.rationale: Pan-Finnic sources make no claims about universal moral truths, and adherents combined Lutheran and romantic-nationalist ethics.

single-common-good.rationale: No source on the idea discusses pluralism versus a single common good; the question is outside its documented content.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred from the idea's own logic that each people deserves a state; not documented as a position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Karelia Society aided Finnic minorities and refugees from Soviet Russia. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

revive-national-language.rationale: Finnish was promoted as the country's first language in universities and the state, though Finnish had not fallen out of use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the anti-socialist, class-collaboration orientation of interwar adherents; no source addresses firm governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not part of the idea; its education interest lay in language and national awakening.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in any source on the idea.

economic-freedom.rationale: The idea does not link economic and political freedom; adherents' economic views are not documented.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: nation-building by state, army and propaganda (Karelia Society) relied on laws, oaths and force, not just rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supporters backed Karelian and Ingrian Finn groups pursuing their own states, but intended them to join Finland, so the stance is qualified.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents sent volunteers abroad without any international mandate.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Romantic nationalism emphasised folk, language and feeling alongside science.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic-national logic of kin-unity, which prioritises the national community; no source mentions benefits.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-nationalist leanings of interwar adherents; welfare conditions are not discussed in the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Karelia Society put nation and kin above class conflict and was hostile to socialism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Kalevala and Karelian heritage are central to the idea; destroying heritage for a goal is contrary to Karelianism.

dominated-front.rationale: The pan-Finnic front is aimed at Russian domination, not at Western powers, so this Third-World-style front does not match; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from the Karelia Society's nationalism and hostility to socialism, which rejected internationalist class organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-nationalist milieu of the movement; sources on the idea do not discuss gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest prohibition is a religious-economic doctrine absent from Lutheran-nationalist pan-Finnicism; inferred disagreement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Pan-Finnicism ranked peoples but did not advocate racial segregation law within states.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Marxism: pan-Finnic nationalists saw the state as a national instrument, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for the idea's peak and has no link to its kinship aims.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic-nation logic that unity rests on shared language and kinship; immigration was not a live issue for the idea.

elite-replacement.rationale: This is a modern conspiracy theory, absent from the idea's historical sources; adherents' fears were of Russia and communism, not demographic replacement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources on the idea.

national-mission.rationale: Topelius wanted Finns to lead a pan-Finnic community, but not to spread a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-nationalist character of the movement; feminist structural analysis does not appear in its sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: No source records pan-Finnic adherents making this claim; they attacked Soviet Russia and socialists, not domestic elites as such.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Some interwar adherents had Nazi ties but no source ties eugenics to the idea.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred; Finnish adherents defended wartime conduct while Russia alleges genocide, which the article notes is disputed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Karelia Society wanted a strong army and an active nation-building state, which exceeds a minimal state; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Finno-Ugric peoples were placed above East Slavs under the Eastern Karelian administration, suggesting separation, but sources do not state a marriage doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Under the Eastern Karelian military administration Finno-Ugric peoples were placed above East Slavs, who were sent to camps.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate, and pan-Finnic nationalists stood outside it as opponents of socialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Colonial-settler analysis is foreign to the idea's sources; its irredentism rests on kin ancestry, not settler framing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal law and religious communities are not an issue the idea addresses.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion is not an issue in the idea, though Lutheran missions did spread it in Karelia.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious-nationalist demand with no relevance to Finnish kinship nationalism; inferred disagreement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Lutheran missions spread the idea; religious instruction in schools unobjectionable to adherents.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine; pan-Finnic nationalists saw the Soviet state as the enemy and would not endorse it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents split: kin to be freed from Russia with their consent claimed, but the Karelia Society turned against democracy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not stated in the idea's sources; its economic side is only the vague kin economic union.

population-transfer.rationale: Russian-speaking residents were classed as an un-national minority and sent to camps in the Continuation War; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kinship wars were private military expeditions into neighbouring territory and so reject non-aggression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred from romantic-nationalist emphasis on peoples' struggle; not stated.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Karelia Society sought strict restrictions on socialists, and Estonia's Vaps Movement was banned after a coup.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Resistance to Russian domination of Finnic kin is central to the idea, which fits freedom as independence from arbitrary external power; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed in the sources on the idea, and adherents split on democracy.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred from anti-communism: Leninist vanguard thinking was the enemy's doctrine for the Karelia Society.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from nothing in the sources: the idea has no stance on social priority, and adherents' politics varied.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing-policy question with no link to the idea.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the order-minded, anti-socialist interwar adherents (Karelia Society against socialists).

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: kin-peoples nationalists wanted their small peoples to grow and would not blame population for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred from the idea's emphasis on kin and language as the basis of unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from nationalist, hierarchical state-building; sortition is never mentioned in the idea's sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Interwar adherents who turned against democracy favoured emergency powers; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic management is not part of the idea; no source links pan-Finnicism to price policy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: adherents' parties and societies were not ruling single-party states, and no source advocates party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Karelia Society wanted a strong national army, not one under a party; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic-national logic that citizenship belongs to kin; naturalisation is not discussed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not a topic in sources on the idea.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Päts proposed a Finnish-Estonian federation in 1940, and the idea seeks union of kin peoples. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Finnish adherents lived under both the tsar and a republic and no source states a view on who commands the forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Finnish Lutheran church is episcopal, but church governance is not part of the idea; no stance can be derived.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred: although Lutheran missions spread the idea, it is a secular ethnic-nationalism and does not call for clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from the Karelia Society's patriotism and anti-socialism; revolutionary defeatism is the opposite of its stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: No source on the idea discusses censorship of the arts; Karelianism itself celebrated folk art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are not discussed in the sources on the idea.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents sought allies like Estonia, Hungary and Germany, and valued military friendship.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is unrelated to the idea's kinship aims.

people-in-arms.rationale: Interwar adherents backed both a stronger regular army (Karelia Society) and volunteer corps, so the idea gives no clear lean on militias versus professionals.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Karelianism romanticised the Karelian countryside as the source of national culture, which supports a rural-moral view; inferred from this romanticism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The oath names Karelia and Ingria, Finnic lands left under Soviet rule by the 1920 border, as the cause members were bound to win back into one Finland.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea was created and led by scholars and students (Castrén, Ahlqvist, the Karelia Society).

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Finno-Ugric peoples were ranked above East Slavs, and Turanist writers claimed future greatness for kin peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the order-minded outlook of interwar adherents; the sources on the idea do not mention capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-nationalist milieu of its adherents; no source discusses sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The idea itself rests on scholarship (philology, linguistics), and Finnish nationalists did not campaign for creationism; inferred disagreement.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-nationalist and Lutheran milieu; the sources on the idea do not discuss it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the idea's kinship basis; Finnish adherents defined the nation by ancestry and language, though citizenship law is not discussed.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Karelia Society supported Finnish-speaking minorities abroad and Finnic minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious minority exemptions are not an issue in the idea's sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: a nationalism built on shared kinship and national awakening values conformity to the national culture over eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is not addressed in the idea's sources.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Development strategy is not part of the idea; nothing links kin unity to rapid growth at the cost of freedom.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred disagreement: pan-Finnic independence aims were political and territorial, not tied to economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred: the idea's solidarity is kin-based and national, not a global duty of aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic for the idea's historical peak and are unrelated to kinship politics.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources on the idea do not address how heads of state are chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary governance is not addressed in the idea's sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Interwar adherents pressed for East Karelia and, after the wars, for the Karelia question, refusing to accept lost lands.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate among Marxists; pan-Finnic nationalists opposed the Soviet state as an enemy regardless of how it is classified.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not addressed in the sources on the idea.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: Finnish adherents rejected Soviet annexation of Karelia, and public opinion favours re-annexing Finnish Karelia.

collective-defense.rationale: Adherents sought friendship and military cooperation with Estonia and Hungary, which fits mutual defence; inferred from that kin-friendship diplomacy.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred disagreement: Lutheran missions helped spread the idea, so supporters did not seek to curb church power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Whether the head of state should be nonpartisan is not discussed in the sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The idea backs kin peoples breaking away from Russia and uniting with Finland, so adherents would not endorse force against secession in general; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy within a larger state is not discussed; the aim was integrating kin into a Greater Finland or independent states.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: a modern national movement with an oath to Fatherland and God, not a divine-descent ruler; sources never mention it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is not addressed by the idea's sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea rests on a primordial view of ethnicity and inherited kinship (Shabaev and Mironova).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the Fennoman tradition's constitutional arguments against Russian rule; no source defends an unbound ruler.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is anachronistic for the idea's historical period and unrelated to its kinship aims.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional theory is not addressed in the sources on the idea.

leader-cult.rationale: The sources on the idea mention flags and oaths but no leader cult; the Karelia Society was a student organisation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family courts are not part of the idea's sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theme; pan-Finnic nationalists rejected socialism and the theory, so disagreement is inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Finnish agrarian reform is not part of pan-Finnic sources, and supporters were not united on land questions.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred: the Karelia Society aided refugees from Soviet Russia and Finnic kin, and Karelian evacuees wished to return, so adherents back return rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Greater Finland's natural borders cover areas inhabited by Finns and Karelians, and kinship is the claim's basis.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred disagreement: Lutheran-national adherents did not call for criminal penalties for leaving religion, and sources never raise it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress codes are unrelated to the idea and alien to Finnish Lutheran culture; inferred disagreement.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not addressed, though kin economic union is part of the definition; no source details a single currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Finnicism is defined as advocating political or economic unification of the Finno-Ugric peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the Karelia Society's support for cultural ties with Finnish-speaking minorities in Sweden and Norway.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Adherents wanted kin peoples under Russia to be independent or join Finland, not just win rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea rests on primordial ethnicity and language as drivers of history, not economics.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed by the idea's sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank rescues are anachronistic and not discussed in the idea's sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the conservative-nationalist milieu; gender quotas are anachronistic for the idea.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The definition mentions kin economic unification, but autarky is not documented as a pan-Finnic aim.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements with social clauses are anachronistic and not addressed by the sources on the idea.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work incentives are not a pan-Finnic topic, though the Karelia Society's oath shows its stress on sacrifice for the nation.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Volunteer expeditions during the kinship wars aimed to spark uprisings among kin under Russian rule, matching a foco-style approach; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Aristocratic titles are not an issue for the idea, which was led by commoner scholars and later students.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Karelianism and Finno-Ugric studies centred the kin peoples' own history, so adherents would favour teaching history around the Finnish and Finnic story; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Topelius saw Finns leading a pan-Finnic community by cultural seniority, and Finland was seen as Estonia's protector.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Karelia Society ran national-awakening propaganda and oaths before the flag, so adherents back patriotic schooling; inferred from these practices.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the movement's ethnic-nationalist, anti-egalitarian outlook; preferences by race are not discussed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform theory is not addressed by the idea's sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Marxist collapse theory by the anti-socialist interwar adherents.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: adherents sought political and cultural influence in Karelia and Ingria, but these were not Finnish possessions, so the match is partial.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theory is anachronistic and not addressed; the idea sought kin union, not economic withdrawal.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory; interwar nationalists were hostile to Marxism, so disagreement is inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Private discrimination law is anachronistic and not discussed by the sources on the idea.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Entrenched rights are not discussed; Fennoman struggles were about autonomy under the tsar.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not documented: Pan-Finnic claims rest on kinship, and the idea's sources do not discuss voiding treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Finland became a republic and supporters of the idea mostly accepted it; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: a nationalist movement building a unified kin state would not grant individuals vetoes over collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Castrén envisioned resisting Russian rule; Fennomans used constitutional arguments.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is not addressed in the sources, and adherents split on democracy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not discussed in sources on the idea.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed; inferred only from the rural, agrarian outlook of Karelianism.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The duty of the wealthy to others is not discussed in sources on the idea.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred disagreement: pan-Finnic adherents were activists who staged expeditions, propaganda and oath rituals.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt-school-style critique absent from the sources on the idea.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian theory that no pan-Finnic source engages; nationalists treated kinship as the unifying force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the idea; its grievance is against Russian rule.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not documented: Finnish adherents defined nationhood by kinship, which suggests office-holding by natives, but no source says so.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist-party question, unrelated to the idea.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The idea says nothing on aid, though an irredentist nationalism would value self-reliance; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Finnish adherents campaign over East Karelia and the Karelia question, which is territory lost to Russia; the Karelia question remains the most realistic goal of Greater Finland.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not documented: the idea treats Finno-Ugric peoples as native to their lands, which suggests support, but the Sami and similar groups are not discussed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Allied commission labelled the Karelia Society fascist and disbanded it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents were fiercely anti-communist, but some leaders of the Karelia Society had ties to National Socialist groups, so adherents did not treat both as equally bad; adherents split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is irrelevant to the idea, and nothing in its sources bears on it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the idea's emphasis on national heritage and flags; monument controversies are not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources on the idea.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources on the idea.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: the idea stresses kin peoples' own culture, which supports distinct civilisational paths, though adherents took European models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the Karelia Society's push for a stronger army and its alliance with ultra-right movements.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the conservative-nationalist view of family; not discussed in the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-Lutheran milieu of its adherents; not discussed in sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not discussed in the idea's sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from nationalist defensiveness; the idea's sources do not discuss company takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed; Lutheran conservative adherents would be split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred disagreement with a council-democracy model that does not fit a nationalist state-building movement.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions are not discussed in the sources on the idea.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred disagreement: Finnish nationalists favoured smallholder property, not communal land tenure subject to withdrawal.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Fiscal oversight is not discussed; adherents were split on democracy.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the push to make Finnish the first language of universities and state; but Swedish remained official, so only a mild lean.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from nationalist concern for kin territory; not documented in sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic US-style civil-rights doctrine, not part of the idea.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the romantic, folk-culture orientation of Karelianism; consumerism is not discussed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Greater Finland supporters backed Karelian and Ingrian groups seeking their own states.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; the idea's allies (Estonia, Hungary) were friendships rather than blocs under one power.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporate lobbying is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist outlook and the Karelia Society's hostility to outside influences; not documented.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: kin peoples were small, and nationalist writers valued growth of the Finnic population; not documented in sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not documented; inferred from nationalist protection of kin territory.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not discussed; employment policy has no link to kinship nationalism.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed; pan-Finnic adherents did not argue from international-relations theory.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the Karelia Society's oath demanded duty to Fatherland and law; but adherents also resisted Russian law.

non-intervention.rationale: Finnish volunteers entered Russian territory during the kinship wars to help kin, contradicting a rule against intervening in other states' affairs.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation form is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The sources show hostility to Russians and socialists but not a claim of a secret minority conspiracy; adherents did not share one.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the conservative Lutheran milieu; marriage law is not discussed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

local-production.rationale: Localism is not part of the idea; its economic side is the vague kin economic union.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the Karelia Society was a formal, hierarchical organisation with oaths and flags.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the idea's sovereignty-minded nationalism; not documented, as international law was thin in its period.

religious-nation.rationale: Kinship in the idea is by language and ancestry, with Castrén extending it to non-Christian Altaic peoples, so religion does not define the nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Topelius wanted Finns to lead a pan-Finnic community, but ritual tribute is a Sinocentric idea absent from the sources.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in sources on the idea.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Karelia Society's slogan targeted socialists, communists and Russians, and the Soviets were the idea's chief opponent.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred disagreement: Lutheran missions spread the idea and the Karelia Society's oath invoked God.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not discussed; the idea's sources lack a view on capitalism as a historical stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred disagreement from a conservative-nationalist milieu with no interest in economic restructuring.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the anti-socialist, family-minded milieu of adherents.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: Fennoman language promotion favoured Finnish vocabulary, but the sources for pan-Finnicism do not describe purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: The idea's sources do not discuss indigenous treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea aims at a large kin-state, not small cooperative communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not documented in the idea's sources: no pan-Finnic text states a policy of settling the majority group among minorities, so no stance is claimed beyond a weak guess.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Pan-Finnicism has no economic third way; adherents opposed communism but had no doctrine on capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Karelianism treated Karelia as the common ancestral home of Finns and Karelians.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a position of the idea; its sources do not mention it, and mainstream adherents would reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the conservative milieu and period; the sources do not discuss it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: the Karelia Society came to oppose democracy and sought strict restrictions on socialists, though adherents were split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Pan-Finnicism concerns kin territories contiguous to Finland, not overseas colonies, so no position follows.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A concept specific to Islamic jurisprudence, irrelevant to the idea.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred disagreement: Lutheran-national adherents did not seek to overthrow rulers for being secular.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred disagreement: adherents were wary of democracy (Karelia Society) and the idea has no participatory element.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred disagreement: a critical-theory concept absent from pan-Finnic sources and incompatible with their kinship-first view.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the conservative milieu; anachronistic for the idea's historical period.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the Lutheran conservative milieu; the sources do not discuss it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not discussed: adherents placed themselves firmly against socialism, which suggests they saw a meaningful divide; no explicit statement.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept not engaged by the idea's sources; inferred disagreement from anti-Marxism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anachronistic: Castrén's Turanism even included Turkic and Muslim peoples as kin, and the Finnish adherents did not discuss Islam as such.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic workplace-law question unrelated to the idea.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic order is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Karelia Society pushed for a stronger army and the idea's goals relied on military force, so adherents would reject abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Not discussed: development sequencing has no link to the idea's sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: adherents sought Estonian, Hungarian and, in the wars, German cooperation, and so did not favour neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea flourished under a republic and a national awakening; dynastic rule is not discussed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is not discussed in the idea's sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not discussed: the sources on the idea do not mention international lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred disagreement: interwar Finland had universal suffrage and the idea's sources do not call for a property franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim absent from the idea's sources; inferred disagreement.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept, absent from pan-Finnic sources; inferred disagreement from anti-Marxism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred disagreement: a Marxist critique of bourgeois liberties that the anti-socialist adherents rejected.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the Fennoman tradition of constitutional arguments against arbitrary tsarist rule; not explicitly stated.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea's sources discuss kinship and language, not restricting votes by race within a state.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed in the sources on the idea.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed in the sources on the idea.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not discussed: Finnish Lutheran adherents did not campaign on interfaith marriage, and kin were defined by language.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not documented: the idea's sources show no campaign of boycotting a religious minority's shops.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred disagreement: a deliberative-democracy device unrelated to a nationalist movement sceptical of democracy.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth concentration is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the conservative milieu; anachronistic for the idea's historical period.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred disagreement: Lutheran missions spread the idea and the Karelia Society's oath invoked God, so state atheism is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred disagreement: a nationalist order-minded movement would not abolish policing; not documented.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not discussed: the idea sought unity in one kin state rather than consociational arrangements.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

term-limits.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred disagreement with a liquid-democracy device that does not fit its sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic and unrelated to the idea's concerns.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the conservative Lutheran milieu of its period; not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the idea's ethnic-nation logic that political membership rests on kinship.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred disagreement from respect for property; intellectual property is not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the Karelia Society's flag-and-oath rituals and paramilitary Civil Guard culture suggest sympathy for uniformed youth, but youth organisation is not documented as a plank.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for the idea's historical period.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not documented: Finnish adherents sought allies but did not debate foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not discussed: Russia alleges genocide in the occupied East Karelia, which the article notes is disputed, so adherents would hardly endorse recognising mass killings by default.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The concept rests on a primordial view of ethnicity with reconstructed ancient common homeland.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the conservative milieu; a modern theory absent from the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred disagreement: a modern feminist debate unrelated to the idea.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Karelia Society members swore to sacrifice work and life for Greater Finland, and honouring those who died for the cause fits this ethos; inferred from the oath.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Karelia Society's oath ties belief in one great God to belief in Greater Finland, giving the cause a quasi-religious tone; only a partial match.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Finland was seen as the protector and cultural leader of kin peoples, fitting a homeland-as-centre model, though territory was also claimed.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Finno-Ugric movement began as a cultural project, and the Karelia Society began as a cultural organization.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist view that kin should hold the economy; not documented in sources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The oath's goal is a single 'great Finland' joining the Finnic lands of Karelia and Ingria to Finland as one state.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is not discussed; interwar adherents opposed socialist unions, so no clear lean.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist definitional question outside the idea's sources.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

second-chamber.rationale: Parliament design is not discussed in the sources on the idea.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred disagreement from anti-socialist, smallholder-friendly outlook.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea sought one kin state or federation led by Finland, not municipal confederations.

family-wage.rationale: Not documented: inferred from conservative family values of the milieu.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the state-security orientation of adherents; anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the Karelia Society oath pledges life to the Fatherland, putting nation over person.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Lutheran milieu and the Karelia Society's oath invoking God; not a core claim.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from unitary-state thinking (Snellman) in the Fennoman tradition; devolution is not discussed.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from Karelianism's rural romanticism, which favours the countryside over dense cities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Turanist writers claimed shared kin interests among Ural-Altaic peoples, but Pan-Finnicism itself is cultural-linguistic, so only a weak match.

racial-pride.rationale: Turanist strands claimed kin greatness and Castrén argued Finns were not a solitary people from the bog; pride in ancestry fits, though race is not systematically discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Greater Finland is irredentist and volunteers launched expeditions into Soviet lands, so adherents did not limit force to defence.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea sought national unity, not separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: interwar adherents saw Soviet Russia as an enemy of Finnic peoples, but a partition plot against Finland is not documented.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; the Karelia Society was a student body but university tuition was not its issue.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the idea's emphasis on national continuity and kin; not directly stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the Karelia Society wanted a stronger army, and territorial aims relied on force.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

capital-controls.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Volunteer corps and expeditions in the kinship wars acted outside the state's army, so adherents did not hold a strict state monopoly; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the Karelia Society's patriotism and the idea's reliance on armed expeditions.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labour relations are not discussed; adherents were split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on the idea.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred disagreement: pan-Finnicism seeks to build or enlarge a state, not smash it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the idea seeks one unified kin state, not communities choosing divergent systems.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Politicians' pay is not discussed in any pan-Finnic source, and adherents' views followed their parties, so no lean is claimed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Interwar adherents defended property against socialism yet put the nation's good above individuals in the Karelia Society oath; the sources do not settle which weighs more.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The statement is Marxist in framing; pan-Finnic sources neither accept nor reject the distinction, and adherents held private property by default.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Karelia Society oath pairs belief in one great God with faith in Greater Finland and Lutheran missions spread the idea, but a doctrine of divine authority is not stated.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: a movement that urged a stronger army and fought kinship wars rejects strict pacifism, though sources do not discuss the ethics of killing.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the Lutheran conservative milieu of adherents; theological language is never discussed in sources on the idea.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the conservative Lutheran milieu; feminist theology is anachronistic for the idea and absent from its sources.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Finnicism treats shared language family and descent as the basis of kinship across state borders, with Castrén's grammars central to the case.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The kinship idea concerns language, descent and territory; it has no stated view on pricing ecosystems, so this is a neutral inference.

sacred-nation.rationale: The oath is sworn by all that is holy and sets faith in one great Finland beside faith in one great God, treating the nation as an object of devotion; whether adherents held it sacred in the full sense is not stated.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Nothing in the movement concerns student finance, and interwar Finnish nationalists had no student loan debates; no lean can be inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The movement framed exploitation as Russian rule over kin peoples, not a rich centre exploiting poorer regions within Finland; it is largely outside its concerns.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The interwar Lutheran and conservative nationalist milieu accepted a common human nature, though the movement ranks peoples by kinship; inferred from that milieu.

public-service-media.rationale: Sources say nothing on broadcasting; Finland founded Yle in 1926 during the heimoaate era, but adherents had no recorded position.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Interwar Finnish nationalists were mostly Lutheran or Orthodox-hostile, and the idea rests on kinship, not religion; inferred only.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the Finnish nationalist milieu of the era, with strong agrarian parties; the idea has no economic doctrine.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the strong security and anti-Russian posture of the Greater Finland current.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Academic Karelia Society programme opposed socialists and put national unity above class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; inferred from nationalist concern for the integrity of the nation.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed, and the interwar nationalist milieu is mixed; no stated lean.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The kinship idea treats Finnic peoples as one language family and nation by descent, so related Karelian and Finnish varieties count as one.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the interwar statist, nation-building milieu, which favours public rules.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the Finnish nationalist commitment to parliamentary national government; chiefs were never an issue.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the doctrine; no lean can be inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed and the idea is not about penal policy; no lean.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the Finnish-language nationalism of the Academic Karelia Society programme, which put the Finnish language at the centre of nationhood.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Kinship nationalism has no labour doctrine; interwar Finnish nationalists were hostile to the left unions but there is no stated view on compulsory dues.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the idea, and the interwar milieu predates modern ID debates.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Kinship by language and descent says nothing on interpretations of religion; Lutheran church standing was assumed and not disputed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents ranged from parliamentary nationalists to authoritarian activists, and no source states a view on what makes a government democratic.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, Lutheran interwar nationalist milieu; the idea itself does not address sexual morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic for a movement peaking in the 1940s; adherents' nationalist and security-minded outlook gives no clear lean.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the agrarian and conservative interwar nationalist milieu, which did not favour such schemes.

women-suffrage.rationale: Finland gave women the vote in 1906 and the idea's adherents did not contest it, but the movement's own sources do not address it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditional, church-friendly nationalism of the milieu, which would reject the claim.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its premise that peoples are natural kin groups by descent and language, which sits poorly with a purely constructed view.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the traditional views on gender roles in the interwar nationalist milieu.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Property acquisition never featured in kinship nationalism; no stated lean.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a nationalism that put national and kin claims first and distrusted outside judgment of its wars.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not addressed directly; Finnish nationalists were mostly Lutheran but the idea itself rested on language and descent, not scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the conservative, male-centred interwar nationalist milieu of the Academic Karelia Society.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Academic Karelia Society's programme was hostile to socialists, and the movement fought Soviet power, so it would oppose defending a Soviet-style planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the society's stance on democracy and its preference for strong national leadership.

national-church-status.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Lutheran, Finnish-language nationalist milieu that tied church and nation.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Greater Finland backed Karelian and Ingrian states for kin peoples, implying self-rule for kin majorities; the exact form is inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Kin-land aims were framed as the peoples' own wish, so a local vote fits, but irredentists favoured force; inferred and contested.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Greater Finland sought to redraw the Russian border; the statement concerns colonial borders, so this is inferred from its general irredentism.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; Greater Finland aimed to settle Finnic kin lands but the indigenous-majority framing is inferred only.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the male-centred military culture of the interwar Finnish nationalist milieu.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Academic Karelia Society oath and flag oath bind members to the fatherland and the kin lands, which centres the duty to protect ancestral land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the legalistic nationalist milieu; the question is anachronistic and sources do not discuss it.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to Russia and later Soviet power; China ties are anachronistic.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Pan-Finnicism holds that Finland should support the Finnic kin peoples in Karelia and neighbouring lands, and the heimosodat were fought for this.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the interwar nationalist milieu; sources do not discuss common ownership of resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its collectivist nationalism, which places the nation above the individual.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The idea has no economic doctrine of its own.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The idea has no welfare doctrine of its own.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred as the movement worked through societies and the state; sources do not discuss bypassing parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: No economic doctrine; adherents are split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Sources do not address denominational politics; adherents are split.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from national romantic appeals to ancestral kinship and heritage within a modern state.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the conservative interwar Finnish nationalist milieu.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from Greater Finland's aim to bring kin lands and their resources under Finnish control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: No economic doctrine; adherents are split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, non-internationalist milieu.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from its race-and-kinship framing and the interwar milieu; sources do not discuss disadvantaged racial groups.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Sources do not address natural-law claims; adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the idea's concerns.

multipolar-world.rationale: Its aim was a Finland-led kin bloc against Russia, not a general multipolar order; inferred and split.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist milieu's rejection of Marxism.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism of kinship, which included ordinary Finns in a national cause.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from its identity-based nationalism, which treats kinship as central.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its strong anti-Soviet and anti-communist stance.

missingStatements.text: Governments should fund cultural and educational ties with related peoples living in other countries.
missingStatements.rationale: The Karelia Society cultivated cultural ties with Finnish-speaking minorities in Sweden and Norway and aided Finnic minorities and refugees, and friendship with Estonia and Hungary.

notes: Hungarian Turanism, the cultural Finno-Ugric congress movement today, and the earlier Fennoman cultural stage would answer some economic and political items differently. Rationales on economic and social items are inferences from the interwar milieu, not from pan-Finnic sources, and the Academic Karelia Society page is a Wikipedia article quoting the oath; no primary document was opened directly.
